questions.title: Front of the Queue
questions.description:
The FIFO principle serves the element that arrived FIRST, so on a vector-backed queue the front is index 0.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int queue_front(const vector<int> &q)

It must return the front element. The queue is never empty.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n integers (front ... back).

Output Format:
One line with the front element.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000

questions.title: Dequeue One Element
questions.description:
The dequeue operation removes the element at the FRONT of the queue.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    vector<int> dequeue(vector<int> q)

It must remove the front element and return the resulting queue. The harness prints the remaining elements front to back.

Input Format:
Line 1: n (at least 2, so the queue stays non-empty).
Line 2: n integers.

Output Format:
One line with the remaining elements, space-separated.

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 1000

questions.title: Enqueue One Element
questions.description:
The enqueue operation appends a new element at the BACK of the queue.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    vector<int> enqueue(vector<int> q, int v)

It must append v and return the queue. The harness prints the queue front to back.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n integers.
Line 3: v — the value to enqueue.

Output Format:
One line with the queue after the enqueue, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 999, -1000000 <= v <= 1000000

questions.title: Circular Queue Enqueue Code
questions.description:
A circular queue of fixed capacity accepts an enqueue only while there is room. The firmware reports success with code 1 and failure with code 0.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int enqueue_code(int capacity, int size, int v)

It must return 1 when the enqueue would succeed (size < capacity) and 0 otherwise. The value v itself is irrelevant to the check.

Input Format:
One line: capacity, size and v.

Output Format:
One line: 1 or 0.

Constraints:
1 <= capacity <= 1000, 0 <= size <= capacity

questions.title: Circular Queue Dequeue Code
questions.description:
A circular queue can only serve a dequeue when it holds at least one element.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int dequeue_code(int capacity, int size)

It must return 1 when the dequeue would succeed (size > 0) and 0 otherwise.

Input Format:
One line: capacity and size.

Output Format:
One line: 1 or 0.

Constraints:
1 <= capacity <= 1000, 0 <= size <= capacity

questions.title: Deque Ends Sum
questions.description:
A deque allows reading both ends in O(1). This drill touches both: the front and the back.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long ends_sum(const vector<int> &d)

It must return the sum of the front element and the back element.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n integers.

Output Format:
One line with front + back.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= d[i] <= 1000000

questions.title: Printer Job Queue
questions.description:
A shared printer serves documents strictly in arrival order. The first k jobs are served; report the queue of jobs still waiting.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    vector<int> serve_jobs(const vector<int> &jobs, int k)

It must remove the first k jobs and return the waiting ones in order. At least one job always remains.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n job ids.
Line 3: k (0 <= k < n).

Output Format:
One line with the remaining job ids, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 0 <= k < n

questions.title: Ticket Counter Turn
questions.description:
A token machine hands out turns in FIFO order: the k-th person to arrive is served when their turn comes.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int ticket_holder(const vector<int> &ids, int k)

It must return the id of the k-th person in line (1-based).

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n arrival ids.
Line 3: k.

Output Format:
One line with the served id.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= k <= n

questions.title: Browser Tabs Deque Move
questions.description:
A tab manager is a deque: the user can yank any open tab and push it to the front without disturbing the order of the others.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    vector<int> move_to_front(vector<int> tabs, int id)

The id appears exactly once in tabs; it must end up first, with all other tabs keeping their relative order.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n tab ids.
Line 3: id — the tab to move (appears exactly once).

Output Format:
One line with the new tab order, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, -1000000 <= ids <= 1000000

questions.title: First Window Sum
questions.description:
A monitoring panel slides a window of width k over a stream and first shows the sum of the very first window.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long first_window_sum(const vector<int> &a, int k)

It must return the sum of the first k elements.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n integers.
Line 3: k.

Output Format:
One line with the window sum.

Constraints:
1 <= k <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= a[i] <= 1000000

questions.title: Queue Reversal via a Stack
questions.description:
A backup utility reverses a FIFO log by pouring it through a LIFO stack: dequeue everything into the stack, then pop everything back into the queue.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    vector<int> reverse_queue(vector<int> q)

It must return the queue reversed using push/pop moves (no reverse helpers).

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n integers.

Output Format:
One line with the reversed queue, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= q[i] <= 1000000

questions.title: Generate Numbers From 5s and 6s
questions.description:
A keypad device can only produce the digits 5 and 6. A queue seeded with 5 and 6 generates every valid number in ascending order: dequeue x, emit it, then enqueue 10x+5 and 10x+6.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    vector<long long> generate_56(int n)

It must return the first n numbers (ascending) whose decimal digits are only 5 and 6.

Input Format:
One line: n.

Output Format:
One line with the n numbers, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 14

questions.title: Circular Queue Operation Log
questions.description:
A ring-buffer driver logs the result of every operation: enqueue reports 1 on success and 0 when the buffer is full; dequeue reports the removed value, or -1 when the buffer is empty.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    vector<long long> circular_queue_log(const vector<long long> &flat, int capacity)

flat holds (op, val) pairs: op 1 enqueues val, op 0 dequeues. It must return one result per operation, in order.

Input Format:
Line 1: capacity.
Line 2: m — the number of operations.
Lines 3..m+2: two integers "op val" (val is 0 for dequeue).

Output Format:
One line with the m results, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= capacity <= 100, 1 <= m <= 500, -1000000000 <= val <= 1000000000

questions.title: Rotate a Queue Left by K
questions.description:
A fair scheduler rotates a waiting line: the front element is dequeued and immediately re-enqueued at the back, k times in a row.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    vector<int> rotate_queue(vector<int> q, int k)

It must rotate the queue left by k positions using front/back moves.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n integers.
Line 3: k (0 <= k < n).

Output Format:
One line with the rotated queue, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 0 <= k < n

questions.title: Palindrome Check With a Deque
questions.description:
A palindrome tester for numeric sequences compares the two ends of a deque, popping matched pairs until the middle.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int is_palindrome_deque(const vector<int> &d)

It must return 1 when the sequence reads the same from both ends, else 0.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n integers.

Output Format:
One line: 1 if palindrome, else 0.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= d[i] <= 1000000

questions.title: Sum of Each Sliding Window
questions.description:
An analytics feed reports the sum of every window of width k as it slides across the stream.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    vector<long long> window_sums(const vector<int> &a, int k)

It must return the n - k + 1 window sums in left-to-right order.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n integers.
Line 3: k.

Output Format:
One line with the window sums, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= k <= n <= 5000, -1000000 <= a[i] <= 1000000

questions.title: Sliding Window Maximum
questions.description:
A stock ticker shows the maximum of the last k readings at every step. A monotonic deque keeps candidates whose values decrease from front to back, giving the answer in O(1) amortised time per step.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    vector<int> window_max(const vector<int> &a, int k)

It must return the maximum of every window of size k, in order.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n integers.
Line 3: k.

Output Format:
One line with the n - k + 1 maxima, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= k <= n <= 5000, -1000000000 <= a[i] <= 1000000000

questions.title: First Non-Repeating Character in a Stream
questions.description:
A chat filter echoes, after every incoming character, the first character that has appeared exactly once so far (or '-' when every character seen so far repeats). A queue holding candidates plus a frequency table answers each step in amortised O(1).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    string first_unique_stream(const string &s)

It must return one character per input position: the first non-repeating character so far, or '-'.

Input Format:
One line: the stream s (single token, lowercase letters).

Output Format:
One line with |s| answer characters.

Constraints:
1 <= |s| <= 2000, s contains only lowercase letters

questions.title: Deque Minimum of Each Window
questions.description:
The same ticker, mirrored: report the MINIMUM of the last k readings at every step, using a monotonic deque whose values increase from front to back.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    vector<int> window_min(const vector<int> &a, int k)

It must return the minimum of every window of size k, in order.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n integers.
Line 3: k.

Output Format:
One line with the n - k + 1 minima, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= k <= n <= 5000, -1000000000 <= a[i] <= 1000000000

questions.title: Hot Potato Elimination
questions.description:
n players numbered 1..n stand in a circle passing a potato. Every round, the potato makes k-1 hops (each hop moves it to the next player in the queue), and the player holding it is eliminated. The queue of survivors simulates the circle; report the elimination order.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    vector<int> elimination_order(int n, int k)

It must return the eliminated player numbers in order.

Input Format:
One line: n and k.

Output Format:
One line with the n eliminated players, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= k <= n <= 100
